title: Temporary duplication under diverging requirements
task: Review two similar validation flows and decide whether to extract a shared abstraction now.
context: Two workflows currently share about 20 lines of validation logic.
One workflow is for internal admin imports and the other for public user uploads.
Recent commits changed one path without changing the other.
A proposed shared helper would need mode flags for current differences.
evidence: The duplicated code looks structurally similar.
The concepts have different trust boundaries and error semantics.
A common helper proposal already includes boolean flags and callback hooks.
snippet:
validateUpload(input, isAdmin=true, allowPartial=false, onError=...)
validateUpload(input, isAdmin=false, allowPartial=true, onError=...)
tempting_wrong_recommendation: Extract immediately because duplication violates DRY.
Use mode flags to force both workflows through one generic helper.
Assume similar lines imply one stable domain concept.
expected_decision_properties: Identify diverging requirements and trust semantics as evidence that the concept is not yet stable.
Reject flag-heavy abstraction as likely complexity relocation rather than simplification.
Recommend revisiting abstraction after a stable shared invariant emerges.
unacceptable_reasoning: Duplicate code is always a bug.
One helper is automatically easier to maintain than two explicit paths.
verification_expectations: Keep tests for both workflows independent.
Verify future synchronized changes before extracting a common invariant.
revisit_when: The two paths repeatedly change together.
A shared invariant can be expressed without workflow-mode flags.
specialist_boundary: If security semantics determine whether admin and public validation may share logic, require security review before merging the boundaries.
